tags.gist: States the principle that whatever verifies a system must stand apart from it structurally, down to the evaluator model itself.
Calls independent third parties structurally necessary for the safety-critical recognition, escalation and calibration elements, where self-assessment cannot resolve the conflict of interest.

Prefers an accreditation structure like ASCA, open to any entity meeting criteria, over a closed panel of named evaluators, to protect competition.
Calls the three approaches necessary but individually insufficient, since each works at a different latency and misses unanticipated, rare or lagging failures.
Adds a fourth approach: continuous verification of every live output against current authoritative sources, logging a citation for each claim cleared or flagged.
Would trigger reassessment on any change to the model or deployment components, while continuous verification makes exact cadence less critical.
Says one passed benchmark run proves little; prefers a reliability profile from repeated runs of reusable, prespecified test bundles.
Supports supervisory agents provided the agent has its own governance, organized in the commenter's build around three loops.
Would trigger reassessment on any change to the model or deployment components, while continuous verification makes the exact cadence matter less.
Says an agent's reliability cannot rest on its own logs; it needs an organizationally and architecturally separate evaluator, or it merely relocates the trust problem.
Suggests naming turn budgets and per-session action or cost caps as a circuit breaker for supervisory agents.
Decomposes the judge into deterministic, semantic, policy and trace evaluators rather than one model judging another.
Suggests that agentic systems be judged postmarket on their full execution path, since endpoint checks miss mid-process failures such as skipped escalation.
Says decomposition reduces the single point of failure, but the chain of supervision must end in a structurally independent, non-agentic check.
Proposes tiering modifications by reversibility and blast radius rather than technical nature, so a prompt change touching escalation may outrank a model swap.
Would let low-tier changes sit in a PCCP with quality-system documentation, while changes touching safety-critical behaviors trigger re-benchmarking before deployment.
Adds mid-session escalation of authority: evaluation should test whether an agent notices when its own available scope expands during a task.
Adds tool-output trust: criteria should distinguish tool outputs from structurally independent sources from those sharing the agent's developer or lineage.
Welcomes CDRH running the process openly and inviting builders, not only manufacturers, and offers further discussion.
